funFact: A common rule of thumb is that a horse should carry no more than about a fifth of its own weight, which is roughly one rider and a saddle.
No ancient writer recorded the horse's weight, so this one is our estimate: a hollow timber horse plus 30 soldiers in bronze armor.
A big mosasaurus weighed about 15 tons, more than two African elephants, and it was a lizard.
Gigantopithecus was the largest ape that ever lived: about 10 feet tall and as heavy as three people.
A fully loaded 747 weighs over 400 tons, and around 40% of that can be fuel.
